reason: Use Tier 2: separate input and output item representations within each SASRec network. The trajectory peaked at 0.5312, then declined after endpoint-weighted supervision; padding corrections and relative-position biases did not recover performance, so further attention refinements have weak empirical support. Tied embeddings may constrain items to share incompatible history-encoding and next-item-retrieval roles; testing this representation hypothesis is distinct from the previous negative-count, weighting, masking, and positional-bias experiments.

plan.model_design: Make one architectural change: add output_emb = nn.Embedding(itemnum + 1, dim, padding_idx=0), retaining item_emb exclusively for sequence inputs. After existing initialization, copy item_emb.weight into output_emb.weight without consuming additional random draws, then train both tables jointly; use output_emb for positive and negative logits in ranking_loss and candidate scores in predict, retaining the existing jointly learned item_bias. This tests whether separating context and retrieval representations improves sparse-item generalization without combining independent predictors. Preserve SASRec constructor arguments, forward(seq), predict(seq, candidates), ranking_loss(seq, pos), existing variable names, relative-position attention, endpoint weighting, NEGATIVES=2048, TOKEN_CAP=2048, sampling, optimizer rules, and all other hyperparameters.
